stem: A kidney transplant candidate has an elevated panel reactive antibody (PRA) screen but no identified donor yet. Which immunologic distinction should the coordinator communicate to the team?

options.text: PRA reflects the percentage of HLA antibodies present, whereas donor-specific antibody (DSA) identifies specific antigens to avoid
PRA and DSA measure identical information and are interchangeable terms
DSA provides only a percentage of sensitization without identifying specific antigens
PRA testing is performed only after transplantation with no pretransplant role

explanation.rationale_correct: A positive crossmatch demonstrates donor-specific HLA antibody. PRA provides the percentage of HLA antibodies an individual has but does not indicate DSA presence; DSA identifies specific antigens to avoid.

rationale_incorrect.B: PRA quantifies overall sensitization while DSA targets donor-mismatched antigens.
rationale_incorrect.C: DSA identifies specific anti-HLA antibodies against donor mismatches rather than only a percentage.
rationale_incorrect.D: PRA and HLA antibody assessment are part of pretransplant immunologic evaluation.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: positive crossmatch … donor-specific HLA antibody (DSA) … PRA provides us with the percentage of HLA antibodies … does not indicate the presence of DSA

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 2 → crossmatch → 7.a.–c. (DSA versus PRA distinction: PRA percentage versus donor-specific antigen identification); PDF p. 74 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. DSA-versus-PRA angle distinct from post-transplant DSA monitoring (cctc-2065) and heart PRA crossmatch threshold (cctc-2026); anchor verified on Cupples p. 74.

stem: When coordinating the laboratory portion of a solid-organ transplant evaluation, which testing category is included in standard assessment references?

options.text: Viral blood studies to determine previous exposures and current immunity
Viral studies only after transplantation with no pretransplant role
Laboratory assessment limited to a complete blood count only
Infectious screening deferred until after waitlist registration only

explanation.rationale_correct: Transplant evaluation laboratory assessment includes viral blood studies to determine previous exposures as well as current immunity, alongside metabolic, hematologic, and disease-screening studies.

rationale_incorrect.B: Viral serologies are part of pretransplant evaluation to guide immunization and infection risk.
rationale_incorrect.C: Evaluation laboratories include comprehensive metabolic, coagulation, viral, and disease-screening studies beyond CBC alone.
rationale_incorrect.D: Infectious and viral studies are obtained during evaluation rather than deferred until after listing alone.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Evaluation → Laboratory assessment → viral blood studies
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Viral blood studies to determine previous exposures as well as current immunity

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → Laboratory assessment (viral blood studies for exposures and immunity); PDF p. 98 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Evaluation viral-studies angle distinct from EBV screening (cctc-2071) and hypercoagulability screening (cctc-2059); anchor verified on Cupples p. 98.

stem: A highly sensitized kidney candidate is approaching a potential transplant offer. When may a prospective crossmatch be performed according to standard immunology references?

options.text: At the time of transplantation based on center- and organ-specific hyperacute rejection risk
Only during the initial outpatient evaluation with no role at transplant
Only after graft implantation is complete
Never for kidney candidates regardless of sensitization

explanation.rationale_correct: A prospective crossmatch may be performed at the time of transplantation based on center- and organ-specific determination of risk of hyperacute rejection, alongside desensitization strategies when indicated.

rationale_incorrect.B: Prospective crossmatch timing at transplantation supplements rather than replaces broader pretransplant antibody assessment.
rationale_incorrect.C: Crossmatch is a pre-implantation immunologic test rather than a post-implantation step.
rationale_incorrect.D: Kidney programs perform prospective crossmatch when hyperacute rejection risk warrants it.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: A prospective crossmatch may be performed at the time of transplantation based on center- and organ-specific determination of risk of hyperacute rejection

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 1 → HLA/sensitization → iii. (prospective crossmatch at transplant based on center risk); PDF p. 27 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Prospective crossmatch timing angle distinct from heart PRA >10% crossmatch (cctc-2026) and DSA-versus-PRA distinction (cctc-2085); anchor verified on Cupples p. 27.

stem: During transplant evaluation, when are biopsies obtained according to standard evaluation references?

options.text: Based on the patient's history and physical examination to confirm disease or determine whether abnormalities are malignant
On every candidate regardless of history or examination findings
Only after transplantation to assess medication adherence
Biopsies are never used during pretransplant evaluation

explanation.rationale_correct: Biopsies are performed based on the patient's history and physical examination to confirm presence or etiology of disease and determine if abnormalities are malignant, which may be a contraindication to transplantation.

rationale_incorrect.B: Biopsies are obtained when history and examination indicate need rather than universally for every candidate.
rationale_incorrect.C: Evaluation biopsies address pretransplant disease assessment rather than post-transplant adherence.
rationale_incorrect.D: Biopsy is listed among evaluation procedures when clinically indicated.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: Biopsies—performed based on patient's history and physical examination to Confirm presence or etiology of disease. Determine if abnormalities are malignant

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → Biopsies (history/physical-driven evaluation to confirm disease or malignancy); PDF p. 98 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Evaluation-biopsy indication angle distinct from liver cardiac stress testing (cctc-2028) and intestinal suitability (cctc-2047); anchor verified on Cupples p. 98.
